text: We finally got the keys to our first house and danced around the empty living room.
my sister just had her baby and i'm an aunt!!! can't stop smiling

Opened the envelope and saw the scholarship letter. I screamed and hugged my mom.
The kids ran into the sea for the first time, shrieking with delight.
Best birthday ever: all my old friends showed up as a surprise.
After months of rehab, she walked across the room on her own and everyone cheered.
The puppy we adopted won't stop wagging its tail when I come home.
We won the neighborhood quiz by one point and celebrated with pizza.
Sun on my face, coffee in hand, nowhere to be. Perfect morning.
He proposed on the beach at sunset and I said yes before he finished the question.
Our band played its first gig and the crowd sang along to every song.
The doctor said the scan is clear. I called everyone I know.
First snow of the year and the kids are building a snowman in pajamas.
My students gave me a card signed by the whole class. Best day of the term.
The garden finally bloomed and the whole street stops to look at the roses.
Got the job! Starting Monday at the place I've wanted to work for years.
We found our lost cat curled up asleep in the neighbor's shed, safe and sound.
The choir hit the last note and the hall exploded in applause.
Dad tasted my cooking and asked for seconds, then thirds.
Reunited with my brother at the airport after five years. We couldn't stop hugging.
The team shipped the app tonight and we're all toasting in the office.
My daughter read her first book out loud and grinned at every page.
Passed the driving test on the first try! Windows down, music up.
The baby laughed for the first time today and we all lost it.
We made it to the top of the mountain just as the clouds cleared.
The bakery's first day sold out before noon. Unbelievable.
Grandma's letter arrived with a photo of all of us from 1998. Pure happiness.
Holidays start tomorrow and the whole family is coming home.
The house feels so quiet since Grandma passed. I keep setting a plate for her.
we put our old dog to sleep this morning. the house is empty without him
I packed the last box from my childhood room after the house was sold, and sat on the floor crying for an hour.
She moved across the ocean today, and I already miss her so much it hurts.
Nobody came to my birthday dinner. I ate the cake alone.
The letter said they went with another candidate. Another no.
Found my late mother's handwriting on a recipe card and cried, because I'll never hear her read it again.
The little bookshop on our street closed for good today.
He forgot our anniversary again. I didn't say anything.
Every year fewer of us gather for the holidays.
The garden my father planted is overgrown now. I can't bring myself to touch it.
My best friend and I don't talk anymore. I still have her number saved.
Rainy Sunday, cold tea, and the photos of everyone I've lost spread across the table.
The vet called: there's nothing more they can do for her.
I moved out of the apartment we shared for ten years and left the key on the counter.
The kids grew up and left. Their rooms are just storage now.
Lost the baby at twelve weeks. We had already picked a name.
The school where I taught for thirty years is being demolished.
Our band played its last show tonight. Half the room was empty.
Dad didn't recognize me today. He asked who I was, politely.
He died in March. I still play his old voicemail just to hear his voice, and it breaks me every time.
The town I grew up in is half abandoned now.
My grandmother's piano was sold, and I wasn't there to say goodbye to it.
the funeral was small. just us and the rain, and nobody could say a word
She said she needs space. I sat in the car and cried for a long time before driving home.
The tree we planted when he was born came down in the storm.
Christmas without Mom. Nobody knew how to make her stuffing.
I failed the exam for the third time and stopped telling people.
Walking past our old café, someone else is sitting at our table.
The last letter from my grandfather arrived a week after his funeral.
They towed my car from my own driveway and want three hundred dollars to give it back!
my coworker took credit for my project in front of the whole board. unbelievable
The landlord raised the rent again and still hasn't fixed the heating.
Somebody keyed my car in the parking lot and drove off.
I waited two hours on hold just for them to hang up on me.
The airline lost my bag and then blamed me for not labeling it.
He lied to my face, again, and acted like I was the crazy one.
They cut down the park's oldest trees overnight without asking anyone.
The referee ignored a blatant foul and the crowd started throwing things.
My neighbor blasts music at 3 a.m. every single night.
The company laid off half of us by email while the CEO got a bonus.
Someone ate my lunch from the office fridge. Again!
The contractor took the money and never came back to finish the roof.
I'm furious: the school punished my kid for something the teacher did.
They charged me twice and now refuse to refund either payment.
He cut in front of the whole line and then yelled at the cashier.
The politician promised to fix the roads and pocketed the budget instead.
My brother sold Mom's ring without telling any of us, and I'm furious.
Stop interrupting me in meetings! I've had enough of it.
The delivery guy threw the package over the fence and broke it.
They fired her for getting pregnant and called it restructuring.
I asked politely three times. Now I'm done being polite.
The bank froze my account for no reason right before rent was due.
Who leaves trash all over a beach and just walks away?
My roommate used my credit card for a party I wasn't even invited to.
The council approved the factory next to the school despite every protest.
He slammed the door in my face after I drove an hour to help him.
The mechanic charged me for parts he never replaced.
they cancelled the show after we drove six hours to see it and won't refund the tickets
Someone hit my bike and rode away laughing.
I heard footsteps behind me in the empty parking garage and started to run.
the doctor wants to see me tomorrow about the results. can't sleep

Something is scratching at the window, and we live on the third floor.
The river is rising fast and the bridge is the only way out.
My son hasn't answered his phone since last night, and I'm terrified something happened to him.
The smoke alarm went off at 3 a.m. and the hallway was full of smoke.
I'm terrified of the surgery on Monday. What if I don't wake up?
The ice cracked under my feet in the middle of the lake.
A man followed me for four blocks and stopped when I stopped.
The brakes stopped working on the steepest part of the hill.
The storm is getting closer and the shelter is full.
My hands are shaking: the biopsy results come out tomorrow.
I woke up to the sound of the front door opening, and I froze, too scared to breathe.
The ground started shaking and the lamps swung from the ceiling.
The dog growled at the empty corner of the room and wouldn't stop, and I was too frightened to turn off the light.
We lost the trail and it's getting dark in the forest.
The car skidded on the ice toward the oncoming truck.
I'm scared to open the mail. I know it's from the bank.
My daughter is lost somewhere in the crowd at the festival.
The elevator stopped between floors and the lights went out.
There's a lump on my neck that wasn't there last week, and I'm scared to call the doctor.
Waiting outside the operating room, every minute feels like an hour.
The wave pulled me out further and I couldn't touch the bottom.
Someone has been calling and hanging up all night, and I'm afraid to be home alone.
The tornado siren is wailing and the sky has turned green.
I'm afraid they'll find out I lied on my application.
the turbulence won't stop and the crew just sat down and buckled in
My heart pounds every time the phone rings since the accident.
